haiku-low.q1: They see the same generic 200 response as every other branch. No row is written and no email is sent.
haiku-low.q2: It is over the limit of three. The generic 200 response is returned, nothing is written, no email is sent, and the existing live link is kept.
haiku-low.q3: It lasts 30 minutes from issue. It ends sooner when used for a successful reset, superseded by a newer link, or revoked after delivery gives up.
haiku-low.q4: Still live. Password rejection happens before the transaction, so the link is not consumed and stays usable until it expires.
haiku-low.q5: No device stays logged in, since all sessions are deleted including the current one. The user is redirected to /login, with no session created, and logs in with the new password.
haiku-low.q6: The worker retries up to three times, then revokes the reset row, logs the failure without the token, alerts ops and drops the job. The user is not told.
haiku-low.q7: The raw token is encrypted with an app key and stored in the email_jobs queue. The worker decrypts it to build the link and deletes the job once sent.
haiku-low.q8: The server hashes the URL token with SHA-256 and looks up the row by the unique token_hash index. It is good only if not consumed, not revoked and not expired.
haiku-low.q9: Not stated as a separate counter. The count comes from password_resets rows filtered by issued_at in the last hour, so older rows fall outside the window.
haiku-low.q10: At issue time, in the same transaction, live links for the user are revoked before the new row is inserted. This does not happen when the request is over the limit.
haiku-low.q11: In one transaction: consumed_at is set, password_hash is updated, sessions are deleted and the password-changed email job is inserted. The email is queued inside that transaction before COMMIT.
haiku-low.q12: The token lookup uses FOR UPDATE plus the live predicate inside the transaction. The losing submit finds no live row and gets the expired page.

sonnet.q1: They see the generic 200 message (same for every branch). Nothing is sent: no row, no email.
sonnet.q2: The fourth request is over the limit (3 or more in the last hour): generic 200, no writes, no email, and the existing live link is kept (not revoked).
sonnet.q3: 30 minutes from issue (expires_at = issued_at + 30 min). It ends sooner if consumed by a successful reset, or revoked (superseded by a newer request, or when email delivery gives up after retries).
sonnet.q4: Still live. The password is rejected before the transaction with a form error, so the link is not consumed and stays live until it expires.
sonnet.q5: None: all sessions for the user are deleted (every device, including the current one), and no session is created. The user is redirected (302) to /login and logs in with the new password.
sonnet.q6: Worker retries with backoff up to 3 times; if still failing it revokes the reset row, logs (no token), alerts ops, and drops the job. The user is not told; they can re-request, which counts against quota.
sonnet.q7: The API generates the raw token and puts it, encrypted with an app key, in the email_jobs payload (with reset_id, address, not_after). The worker uses it to build the link in the email; the job is deleted once sent.
sonnet.q8: The server hashes T with SHA-256 and looks up the row by the unique index on token_hash. It is good if the row is live: consumed_at IS NULL, revoked_at IS NULL and expires_at > now(). Otherwise it shows the expired page. No DB write on GET.
sonnet.q9: It is not stored separately: it counts password_resets rows by issued_at in the last hour (revoked rows still count). Old requests drop out as their issued_at passes the one-hour window (rolling); rows are also purged about a day after expires_at.
sonnet.q10: At issue time, in the same transaction (step 5, before inserting the new row), all of the user's live links are revoked (revoked_at set). This happens only if under the limit; over the limit nothing is revoked.
sonnet.q11: In one transaction: consumed_at set on the reset row, users.password_hash updated, all the user's sessions deleted, and the password-changed email job inserted into email_jobs, all before COMMIT. So the notice is queued within the same transaction as the changes.
sonnet.q12: Inside the transaction, the row is selected with FOR UPDATE and the live predicate (token_hash match and live). The loser finds no live row after the winner commits (consumed_at set), rolls back and gets the expired page.
